name: Moiré stem gauge
subtitle: a trunk clip that shows a thirsty tree

effects.effect: two overlaid fine patterns make broad bands that magnify a small shift

effect: two overlaid fine patterns make broad bands that magnify a small shift
how: Orchards waste water by irrigating on a schedule, and the electronic gauges that show when a tree actually needs water cost too much for most growers. A tree's trunk shrinks by a hair's width during the day when it is short of water; a clip around the trunk overlays two fine-line prints that turn that shrinkage into broad stripes sliding by centimetres (moiré), easy to read by eye or with a phone.
obstacle: Trunks also swell with growth and temperature, so readings must be corrected for both, as the costly gauges do.
why: Farming uses most of the world's fresh water; watering only when trees need it saves much of it.
real: Dendrometers for irrigation scheduling are commercial and moire displacement amplification exists elsewhere, but no moire-based trunk/stem dendrometer was found.
